limitations: Three baseline/candidate process pairs alternate revision order inside one root-coordinated owned-workload quiet interval. OS background activity remains uncontrolled.
Only the calling thread CPU isolates foreground stage work. Process CPU includes other threads in this process.
The AccessKit export stage includes another delta computation; do not add its timing to the separate NodeMap delta stage as if they were disjoint work.
The two steady frames and queued reclaim stage combines frame work and deferred destructors; it is not isolated destructor latency or a native worker scheduler measurement.

Rust requested-payload counters exclude allocator overhead, native allocations, provider/consumer retention, and app RSS. Realloc events overlap alloc/free events; transient old+new storage inside System.realloc is unobserved.
Allocation run instrumented clocks are intentionally removed from comparison; every scalar payload snapshot is captured before reporting JSON allocation.
Changed monolithic logical snapshots still require linear comparisons and removals. This patch does not add persistent per-branch catalogs or skip offscreen accessibility semantics.
These stages identify framework API costs and cannot establish an overall framework CPU/RSS ranking or native end-to-end gain.
